KnightLoader opens RSDF and CCF containers itself, moves your setup over from JDownloader, talks to every debrid service directly and has been through a security pass over the whole code. Every change is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## ✨ Added

- **RSDF and CCF without JDownloader.** KnightLoader opens these containers itself. A `.dlc` still goes to JDownloader, because its key is only handed to registered clients.
- **Move over from JDownloader.** A card under Settings, General takes over accounts, Packagizer and filter rules, archive passwords and the open download list from a JDownloader cfg folder. A preview shows every item before anything is written.
- **Share links to the Android app.** KnightLoader shows up in Android's share sheet and puts the links in the collector of the instance you tap. A `.txt` shared from a file manager is read for its links.
- **Your own servers on the Accounts page.** The Own servers card takes the hostname, username and password of an FTP, SFTP or WebDAV server. A link pasted into the hostname field is cut down to the hostname.
- **A test captcha.** Settings, Captcha sends a captcha KnightLoader draws itself, so you can see how it reaches the window, the phone and your event targets.
- **Torrents through Linksnappy.** Linksnappy fetches magnet links and `.torrent` files like the other debrid services. Rank it above the built-in torrent client on the Accounts page and it takes them. ([#61](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/61))
- **MyDebrid.** KnightLoader talks to MyDebrid directly, with the username and password of your MyDebrid account. The Accounts page shows the plan and when it runs out. MyDebrid does not take torrents.
- **ParleyPort on the Apps page.** The "On a server" card offers [ParleyPort](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport), the relay you can run yourself, next to Unraid, Docker and the source code.

## 🎨 Design

- The README shows each way to run KnightLoader in a picture of its own: desktop, server, Android and the browser extension.
- New pictures for Google Play and F-Droid: five dark screenshots of the app in a drawn phone, each under a short caption, and a new feature graphic, in German and English.
- The Apps page follows the README's order: the server or desktop app first, then the phone app and the browser extension, with the bookmarklet last.
- The README's download buttons stand in groups, the server first, with more room between groups than between rows. Each mark sits nearer the left edge, and ParleyPort's logo is white like the others. The comparison with other download managers has a section of its own after the screenshots, and the screenshots show the container first.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The duplicate check knows the download history.** A link you already downloaded goes to the rejected links with the name and date of that download. Restore adds it anyway, and a switch under Settings, Link collector turns the check off.
- **Every debrid service is KnightLoader's own.** Multihosters reached through JDownloader are gone from the debrid card and the hoster login picker. LeechAll has no public API and asks for a captcha at sign-in, so it is not supported.
- **The relay is ParleyPort.** Instances, the phone app and the browser extension reach the project relay at `parleyport.halleluja.design`. The old address keeps answering for a while.
- **The phone app follows an instance's own relay** when it scans the QR code, and only over `wss://`. It sends nothing unencrypted: a connection saved before 1.5.0 that points at an `http://` address asks to be added again with the twelve words.
- **An instance without a password answers only on names it knows,** so a web page can no longer reach it through DNS rebinding. If you open a passwordless instance through your own domain, add that domain under Settings > Remote access.
- **Sign-in is harder to guess through.** Changing the password signs out every other browser, the attempt limit holds against parallel tries, request bodies have a size limit and idle connections are dropped.
- **Crawls and feeds stay inside the network of the address you entered,** and the relay and the pairing trust only sealed announcements. The app takes a relay peer's name only from its seal.
- **Passwords of hosters and debrid services stay out of logs,** task errors and the diagnostics bundle. A damaged `settings.json`, `accounts.json` or key file is kept as a copy instead of being replaced.
- **FTP, SFTP and WebDAV links are found** in the paste box, uploaded link lists and Click'n'Load.
- **Servers that turn download programs away.** When a server hangs up on the browser agent, KnightLoader asks again as itself. If that fails too, the error says the server closed the connection. The link check also finds the size of links whose server hangs up on a HEAD request.
- **A paused download carries on after a restart** from the bytes already on disk, as long as the server sends the file in parts.
- **Long lines of links read fast.** 8,000 links on one line took close to a minute and now take a fraction of a second.
- **The Android app names none of Google's classes,** so F-Droid can build it. It asks for the camera itself, and the store texts and pictures sit in `fastlane/`, where F-Droid looks. Every store lists the app as just KnightLoader.
- **Captcha solvers are called captcha accounts,** in every language and in the phone app. Buy Me a Coffee opens in the phone's browser, and the store description names who runs the default relay and what answering a captcha loads.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Linksnappy takes links under a hoster's other domains,** such as mega.nz, k2s.cc, ddownload.com or rg.to. Every debrid service now recognises a hoster by all of its known domains. ([#68](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/68))
- Removing a yt-dlp download with its files deletes the video, its partial files and the thumbnail, subtitle and info files, also after a restart, and stops a running ffmpeg without leaving a zombie process in the container. Pause and remove work again after an account change, and subtitles from a site that only has WebVTT are saved as .srt.
- FTP and SFTP downloads delete only their own files, keep their own part file across a restart, resume after an Undo, and can still be paused and removed after an account change. FTPS works with vsftpd, ProFTPD and FileZilla Server, and a password in a link is never saved.
- Removing or restarting a renamed or moved download no longer deletes another download's file at the old place, and a finished download of unknown size is deleted with its files after a restart.
- Pausing or removing a download while its link resolves holds, and a download running when KnightLoader stops comes back queued. A link's size survives a restart.
- A torrent the built-in client has partly fetched keeps its progress after a restart instead of going to a debrid service.
- The end-of-queue action waits for files that are still being checked or moved and for pending retries. Schedules catch up after the computer has slept.
- A package named `..` cannot put files outside the download folder, and unpacking leaves archives that were already in a folder alone.
- Adding a link you already downloaded leaves the finished copy in its package.
- Links in a `.txt` in the watched folder lose the full stop or bracket around them, and control characters in a link no longer end up in a file name.
- The Accounts page loads at once, and captcha accounts show their services' logos, in the dark theme too.
- A failed TorBox web download ends instead of being asked about forever, and a changed hoster login reaches JDownloader.
- The quick-add page waits for Add instead of queuing the links as soon as it opens.
- The browser extension keeps the phrase out of reach of web pages, and several extension sessions no longer push each other out.
- The Windows desktop app writes its log again, and releases reach the Chrome Web Store.
- The Android app's Add links says why a send failed.

## 🌐 Translations

- Every new text is in all 42 languages.
